topic: Nothing about Norway is hard except the language
text:
Norway passes every test a Danish IB student would apply to a destination. No tuition, an hour from Copenhagen, a qualification that converts cleanly, a familiar culture and favourable SU treatment. And then most students discover that several of the largest universities teach no bachelor programme in English at all.

The useful way to read that is not as a closed door but as a choice with a known price. For an IB applicant, Samordna opptak counts Danish A at grade 3 or better as documented Norwegian, and a Danish speaker reads Norwegian from the first day. Doing so turns Norway from a handful of English-taught programmes into an entire national system, free of charge. A student who will not is choosing between a very small number of options.
attribution: This project’s own survey of Norwegian bachelor provision, September 2026
whatThisIsNot: Not a claim about master’s level, where Norway is substantially English-taught. Most confusion about Norway comes from advice written about master’s degrees.
